email.body1:
Miller, saw FloQast crossed $200M ARR on enterprise momentum and the new auditable AI agents.

At that pace, inside sales usually has more in-market accounts than the team can touch before new reps ramp, and that is where pipeline goes cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for FloQast off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Miller, quick follow-up for FloQast.

At $200M ARR with enterprise pulling, the pipeline target on inside sales climbs faster than headcount can. Most managers don't actually know how many meetings the team needs booked to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late in the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your team needs to hit target, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Miller, last bit of proof for FloQast.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your reply rate likely compares to other scaled fintech sales teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Miller, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling inside-sales pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Pushing past $200M ARR is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an inside-sales motion? I'll tailor it to FloQast either way.
